flagged.evidence: The proof says, “A singular chain has compact image and therefore meets only finitely many sheets, so the finite-chain Mayer–Vietoris sequences pass to the direct limit.” The cited Mayer–Vietoris theorem supplies exactness for open covers, but the proof does not establish exactness of the filtered direct limit or justify the resulting kernel/image passage. Exactness of filtered colimits of abelian groups, or a finite-stage argument, would close this short gap.

The proof says, “Place nested disks at distinct nearby heights in that order; their interiors are then pairwise disjoint as subsets of S³.” Its disk-region supplier and algorithm provide planar disks and this height-placement instruction, but do not describe a boundary-fixed embedding: the disk boundaries must remain in the projection sphere for the bands to attach. Smooth height functions vanishing on each boundary and ordered to separate nested sheets would close this short gap.

The entry labels Conway’s work “Matrix Annals 2016 (arXiv:1903.04477).” The official MATRIX listing identifies the chapter as part of the “2019–20 MATRIX Annals,” pp. 31–56 (2021), so the recorded venue/year is inaccurate. [Official MATRIX listing](https://www.matrix-inst.org.au/2019-matrix-annals/).
